context.mainQuestion: Which hypothetical service plan meets workload needs?
context.governingAnswer: Choose Flex for the current non-deferrable peak; reconsider Core only in a different demand scenario.

executiveSummaryDecision.rationale: The final page synthesizes the supported choice for this short example.

synthesisGroups.governingAnswer: Choose Flex for the current non-deferrable peak; reconsider Core only in a different demand scenario.

evidence.text: Synthetic demonstration: Core costs 40 units monthly for 100 jobs; Flex costs 65 units monthly for 180 jobs. Both include monitoring. Core support is next-day; Flex includes same-day support.
evidence.source: Synthetic fixture, not real vendor data

evidence.text: Synthetic demonstration: Normal workload is 80 jobs monthly; peak workload is 140. Excess jobs cannot be deferred in this scenario.

slides.title: Flex covers peak demand at a 25-unit monthly premium
slides.source: Source: synthetic demonstration assumptions; not real vendor data

argument.question: Which plan meets demand at an acceptable cost?
argument.answer: Flex covers the non-deferrable peak; Core only covers normal demand.
argument.interpretation: Choose Flex if the peak is a binding requirement.
argument.qualification: No claim about real vendors or observed demand.

bindings.text:
Core meets the normal 80-job workload at the lower price. Its capacity falls 40 jobs below the 140-job peak scenario, so the cheaper plan cannot satisfy the stated requirement when demand rises.

Flex costs 25 units more each month and adds 80 jobs of capacity. The premium buys sufficient peak coverage and faster support. Core is an alternative only in a different scenario where peak work can be deferred or avoided; that is not the current assumption.
